items.text: Inverse limits in $T(C)$
$R\in\Delta_D$, $T=T_R$, $\delta$ a type of inverse limits; assume (a) limits of type $\delta$ exist in $C$, (b) direct limits of type $D »$ in $C$ commute with inverse limits of type $\delta$.
\text{then in } T(C)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_\Delta(R,C):\quad \varprojlim_\delta\varphi_i\ \text{exists, computed argumentwise}
Proof: it suffices that $\varphi=\varprojlim\varphi_i$ (taken in $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(R,C)$) again commutes with limits of type $D'$ and $D »$.
Type $D'$: clear. Type $D »$: by hypothesis (b).
T\to T'\ \text{(representable)}\ \Longrightarrow\ T(C)\to T'(C)\ \text{commutes with limits of type } \delta
r\in R:\quad r_C\colon T(C)\to C\ \ \text{commutes with inverse limits of type }\delta
Often no limits at all in $T(C)$: e.g. torsors under a fixed group — no sums, products, final or initial object.
Case $D »=\varnothing$: condition (b) empty. If limits of type $\delta$ exist in $C$, they exist in $T(C)$.
$C$ with arbitrary inverse limits: $T(C)$ stable under arbitrary inverse limits.
Change of $\Delta$
Groups: weakest $\Delta$ = categories with finite products; or finite inverse limits; or all small inverse limits (smaller $\Delta$, more exactness).
\Delta'\subset\Delta,\qquad T\ \mapsto\ T|_{\Delta'}\quad(\text{restriction of pseudofunctors})
Restriction sends algebraic theories over $\Delta$ to algebraic theories over $\Delta'$: the stepwise construction restricts. (Tautology, before any universal problem.)
Representable to representable?
T_R|_{\Delta'}\simeq T_{R'},\quad C'\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_\Delta(R,C')\simeq\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\Delta'}(R',C')
Need a universal $\Delta$-functor $R\to R'$ with $R'\in\Delta'$: the $\Delta$–$\Delta'$ envelope of $R$.
If problems 1 and 2 are solvable in $\Delta'$, so is this one.
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\Delta}(R,C')\ \subset\ \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathbf{Cat}}(R,C')\simeq\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\Delta'}(\Delta'(R),C')
$\Delta'(R)$: the $\Delta'$-envelope of the bare category $R$.
$\Delta'\subset\Delta$ means $D\subset D'$ (more limits required in $\Delta'$).
Keep those $\Delta'$-functors $\Delta'(R)\to C'$ commuting with limits of type $D$: impose that the arrows measuring the lack of commutation become isomorphisms (problem 2).
Algebraic theories $\leftrightarrow$ algebraic objects of $\Delta$, and likewise for $\Delta'$.
Warning
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(T_1,T_2)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(T_1',T_2')\quad\text{neither faithful, full, nor essentially surjective}
Homomorphisms of theories depend essentially on the choice of $\Delta$.
The case $D »=\varnothing$
One type of inverse limits, no exactness properties. Next time: $\Delta=$ topoi, pseudo-topoi.
(a) solve problems 1 and 2; characterise $I\to R$ basic (index set of base elements of $T_R$).
(b) structures of type $T_R$ deduced from the same structures in $\mathbf{Sets}$.
\text{structure of type } T \text{ on } X\ \longleftrightarrow\ \text{structure of type } T\text{ on } \operatorname{Hom}(Z,X)
Universal problems, $D'$ = all small diagrams
$\Delta=$ ($\mathcal U$-)categories with all small inverse limits. Despite $D'$ large, no cardinal difficulty.
Problem 1
$I$ a small category; map $I$ universally to a category with arbitrary inverse limits. Dual: $J=I^\circ$ into a category with direct limits.
\widehat J=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(J^\circ,\mathbf{Sets}),\qquad J\hookrightarrow\widehat J\ \text{(fully faithful, Yoneda)}
F\in\widehat J:\quad F=\varinjlim_{(X\to F)\in J/F}X
\varphi\colon J\to D\ \Rightarrow\ \hat\varphi(F)=\varinjlim_{J/F}\varphi(X)
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(J,D)\xrightarrow{\ \hat{\ }\ }\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\Delta}(\widehat J,D)\quad\text{quasi-inverse to restriction}
(Implicit in the SGA 4 treatment of continuous functors; no proof given.)
\text{solution of problem 1:}\quad I\hookrightarrow \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(I,\mathbf{Sets})^{\circ}
$i\mapsto$ the functor it represents; this adds arbitrary inverse limits.
Problem 2
$C$ with arbitrary inverse limits, $\Sigma$ a set of arrows to invert. (Equalising pairs reduces to this: kernels are in $D'$.)
Claim: $C[\Sigma^{-1}]$, computed in $\mathbf{Cat}$, lies in $\Delta$ and $C\to C[\Sigma^{-1}]$ is a $\Delta$-functor.
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_\Delta\big(C[\Sigma^{-1}],C'\big)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\Delta,\Sigma}(C,C')
To check: a functor out of $C[\Sigma^{-1}]$ commutes with inverse limits iff the composite with $C\to C[\Sigma^{-1}]$ does.
Saturating $\Sigma$
\Sigma'=\{u\ :\ \text{every } \Delta\text{-functor } C\to C' \text{ inverting } \Sigma \text{ inverts } u\}
Properties of $\Sigma'$:
1. Stable under composition; contains the isomorphisms.
2. Stable under base change.
3.\ \ \text{two of } u,\ v,\ vu\in\Sigma'\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{the third}
u\colon X\to Y\in\Sigma'\ \Rightarrow\ X\times_YX\to Y\in\Sigma'\ \Rightarrow\ \delta_u\colon X\to X\times_YX\in\Sigma'
Left calculus of fractions
Completion of a span by a fibre product, with the new arrow in $\Sigma'$.
Equalisation: if $f,g$ become equal after composing with $s\in\Sigma'$, take the kernel of the pair: a morphism in $\Sigma'$ equalising them.
\operatorname{Hom}_{C[\Sigma'^{-1}]}(X,Y)=\varinjlim_{(X'\to X)\in\Sigma'/X}\operatorname{Hom}_C(X',Y)
Same objects as $C$; like a calculus of fractions in a ring.
Finite inverse limits: exist in $C[\Sigma'^{-1}]$ and $C\to C[\Sigma'^{-1}]$ is left exact.
Fourth condition
X_i\to Y\ \text{in}\ \Sigma'\ (i\in I)\ \Longrightarrow\ \prod_{i,\,Y}X_i\to Y\in\Sigma'
$\Sigma'$ has it: a functor commuting with infinite fibre products inverts it.
Arbitrary products in $C[\Sigma'^{-1}]$: take $\prod X_i$ in $C$ with its projections, show it is a product in $C[\Sigma'^{-1}]$.
